# 3. Quantitative averaging on a short macro interval

Consider a time-dependent operator
\[
A(t)=\rho\bigl(a^{ij}(t,x)\partial_{ij}
                 +b^i(t,x)\partial_i+c(t,x)\bigr)
\]
with scalar principal coefficient, ellipticity constant \(\lambda_0>0\), and fixed-order spatial coefficient bound \(K\).

Differentiated energy estimates give
\[
\frac{d}{dt}\|z\|_{H^m}^2
+c\rho\lambda_0\|z\|_{H^{m+1}}^2
\le
C_m\rho\left(K+\frac{K^2}{\lambda_0}\right)\|z\|_{H^m}^2.         \tag{3.1}
\]
They require no time derivatives of the coefficients.

On intervals sufficiently short that the growth factor in (3.1) is at most two, weighted energy estimates give
\[
\|S(t,s)\|_{H^{m-r}\to H^m}
\le C_r[\rho\lambda_0(t-s)]^{-r/2}.                              \tag{3.2}
\]
For negative indices, apply the same calculation to the backward adjoint and use duality. Fourier Galerkin approximation justifies these estimates for measurable coefficient schedules.

## 3.1 Consistency and the two-sided telescope

Let a complete microcycle have length \(\ell\), with propagator \(U_\ell\), and first suppose its average is exactly \(\overline A\). Twice using the integral equation gives
\[
\|U_\ell-e^{\ell\overline A}\|_{H^{m+4}\to H^m}
\le C(\rho K)^2\ell^2,                                          \tag{3.3}
\]
and
\[
\|U_\ell-e^{\ell\overline A}\|_{H^m\to H^{m-4}}
\le C(\rho K)^2\ell^2.                                          \tag{3.4}
\]

For \(T_b=n\ell\), telescope
\[
U_\ell^n-e^{T_b\overline A}
=
\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}
U_\ell^{n-1-j}
  (U_\ell-e^{\ell\overline A})
e^{j\ell\overline A}.                                           \tag{3.5}
\]

For the first half of the sum, use (3.4) and recover four derivatives with the actual future propagator. For the second half, use heat smoothing on the right and then (3.3). Each smoothing interval has length comparable to \(T_b\). Consequently,
\[
\|U_\ell^n-e^{T_b\overline A}\|_{H^m\to H^m}
\le C K^2\lambda_0^{-2}\frac{\ell}{T_b},
\qquad m=0,1.                                                   \tag{3.6}
\]

This avoids assuming operator-norm continuity at time zero on an \(H^1\) ball.

## 3.2 Inserting velocity resets

Insert a velocity reset after every excursion. Suppose the reset occupies at most a fraction \(\beta\) of the excursion duration.
